title: stepUp/stepDown shouldn't preserve empty value

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-stepdown

> 10. If either the method invoked was the stepDown\(\) method and value is greater than valueBeforeStepping, or the method invoked was the stepUp\(\) method and value is less than valueBeforeStepping, then return\.

If the value before stepping was the empty string, valueBeforeStepping will be 0.  But this leads to surprising behaviour.

Suppose a number input has a positive value for 'min' and an empty value.  By spec, stepDown() will not change the value because valueBeforeStepping (which is 0) is less than the positive minimum.  If the initial value had really been '0' this would be the desired behaviour, as explained in the spec's example.  But since the initial value was empty, this is not a case of stepDown() increasing the value.  (In this example, stepUp() would set the value to the minimum.)

I think step 10 should apply only if the initial value was not the empty string, so in the example above stepDown() would set the value to the minimum (just as stepUp() would).

Firefox currently implements the behaviour I expected: it obeys step 10 only if the value before stepping was non-empty.  This is mostly consistent with how the UI spinbox buttons work too.  (The spinbox buttons work differently depending on whether the textbox is empty or the user-entered text is non-empty but not a valid number, but the element's value is "" in both cases so the stepUp/stepDown methods do not distinguish between these cases.)

Chrome does not currently seem to obey step 10 at all.  However, its UI spinbox buttons won't change the value in the wrong direction.  I have not tested other browsers.
